title: What this means for energy traders — Thursday, September 24, 2026

sections.overall: Two threads dominate today: the Iran/Saudi disruption narrative in crude and shipping, and the political fight over a possible US diesel export ban. Oil swung on hopes for US-Iran diplomacy even as Saudi Arabia plugs the Asia supply gap left by the East-West pipeline outage, while the diesel-ban debate has now drawn in the EU government and US business groups pushing back on the White House. Underneath that noise, company-level activity keeps building LNG supply relationships with Asian buyers and corporate carbon removal offtake, both confirmed rising trends this week.
sections.CRUDE_OIL: Price action stayed choppy on Iran-talks headlines, with reports of Asia heading for its highest crude imports since the war began cited as a factor in Thursday's move (CNBC). Saudi Arabia has sold almost 100 million barrels to Asian refiners since mid-September to work around the East-West pipeline disruption, with cargoes running into October and November (Rigzone).
sections.NATURAL_GAS: The LNG-Asia offtake trend is the clearest signal in gas this week — Venture Global, BP, Glencore, Equinor, Eni and Petronas have all struck or expanded Asian-facing deals over the past two weeks, and the company count moved from 3 to 4. US LNG capacity headlines have thinned (Cheniere's Corpus Christi Stage 4 draft review and Glenfarne's Magnolia FERC extension were the only US permitting news this week), even as construction continues — Woodside reported its first Louisiana LNG storage tank taking shape. Worth watching: TotalEnergies and ExxonMobil both advanced African gas-to-LNG feedstock projects (Nigeria and Mozambique) on the same day, a possible early sign of renewed IOC interest in African LNG supply.
sections.REFINED_PRODUCTS: Diesel is the most contentious issue in the feed. The White House's proposed 90-day export ban has drawn opposition from US business groups (citing a $6.51/gallon national average, per AAA) and from the EU, which says the move would raise fuel costs on both sides of the Atlantic. EIA data separately shows US retail diesel at $6.29/gallon as of September 14 — the highest nominal price the agency has recorded since it began tracking the series in 1994 — reflecting tight distillate supply and elevated crude costs, a dynamic that predates the export-ban proposal.
sections.CARBON_CREDITS: Corporate offtake activity keeps expanding: Salesforce joined Google and Microsoft as a buyer from Mombak's Amazon reforestation fund, and Google helped structure Symbiosis Coalition offtakes covering more than 40 million tons of nature-based removal. Microsoft and Relae also published a sixth edition of CDR quality criteria addressing delivery risk. Separately, the EU said its planned 250-million-tonne domestic carbon removal purchase program will be kept separate from international credits.
